name: Dia Compe 505Q brake caliper - silver / front
description:
The Dia-Compe 505Q is a high-quality, lightweight brake designed specifically for vintage bikes.
Crafted from cold-forged aluminum, the 505Q has a reach of 45-57mm and delivers reliable stopping power with minimal flex. It features a twist-style quick release for fast wheel changes, and comes in your choice of polished silver or anodized black.
Weighing in at just 146g, this brake combines modern performance, classic aesthetics, and compatibility with a wide range of vintage frames.
ⓘ  Please note: These calipers have an old school nutted mount— NOT A RECESSED NUT —and it is not our fault if you don't read this or look at the photos and order a caliper won't work with your frame and/or fork.

name: Tektro R559 long reach brake caliper - black / front
spec_notes: dual-pivot design w/ forged aluminum arms
description:
You'll never need this much reach on a typical track bike but if you're riding a MASH Steel or Veloci Old Street with big tires and don't want to use a cantilever brake, the R559 is a high quality long reach dual-pull caliper with refillable cartridge-type brake pads.
This is also what you'll probably need if you've converted an old road frame designed for using 27" wheels to 700c.
However, it's a few hairs too short to use on a Skream Ranger fork. For a Ranger front brake, you'll need the  Dia-Compe BRS-202 .

name: Dia-Compe Gran Compe Shot lever - black
description:
The Shot-lever is a magical device that uses two levers to actuate a single brake.
It can be mounted on the left side of the stem or on the right by flipping it over, but please don't be a kook and mount the damn thing backward (the long lever extends past the stem clamp to be used on one side and the shorter one is used on the other side, as pictured here).
